title: Power Automate Pricing: Plans & Costs in 2026
summary: Power automate pricing structures determine the monthly budget required for your organization's specific automation needs and scale of operation.
body_markdown:
## Power Automate hidden costs and request limits


Beyond the sticker price, organizations face strict Power Platform Request limits. These limits throttle high-volume workflows by capping the number of actions, connectors, and API calls a single process can execute within a 24-hour window.


### Power Platform Request Limits and Throttling


The license assigned to a workflow dictates its daily ceiling for operations, creating a performance bottleneck for users who scale without upgrading their plan.


Under a Premium User license, Microsoft limits a single account to **40,000 requests per day** , creating a hard ceiling on the automation volume a single employee can trigger.


If a high-frequency synchronization task between a CRM and a database processes more than one record every two seconds, it will likely fail by mid-afternoon.


To move past this, organizations must purchase the Process License which grants[250,000](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/power-automate-licensing/types) requests per day, effectively allowing for a sixfold increase in automated workflow capacity.


This provides the necessary overhead for mission-critical bots to run continuously without being stopped by the platform’s protective throttling mechanisms.


### AI Builder credit pricing and generative AI costs


Microsoft’s automation intelligence relies a credit-based system that forces a choice between entry-level accessibility and production-grade reliability. While the 2026 tiers include a baseline of 5,000 AI Builder credits, approximately 1,000 standard invoices exhaust this amount.


Unless they buy $500 add-on packs, a growing accounts payable department will face immediate service interruptions.


This math becomes even more volatile when integrating modern LLMs like[Claude Sonnet 5.5](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview) for intelligent document analysis or Gemini 3.8 Flash for high-speed data extraction. Microsoft bills the token consumption of these models on top of the base platform costs.

This disparity shows that the platform prioritizes infrastructure isolation over intelligence capacity in its pricing strategy.


### Dataverse storage capacity overage costs


Storage costs in the Power Platform function as a recurring tax on historical data retention.


Because Dataverse allocates only 10GB of initial capacity, a developer building a high-volume logging system will find that a single year of detailed execution logs can trigger overage charges of **$40 per GB, per month** .


> Storage costs in the Power Platform function as a recurring tax on historical data retention.


This forces teams to either pay a premium for database growth or invest additional engineering hours into building custom archival scripts to offload data to cheaper, external environments.


Regulated and public-sector organizations often bypass these storage and sovereignty bottlenecks by running the air-gapped edition of Activepieces.


The self-hosted enterprise feature list (including SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, and audit logs) matches the managed cloud version exactly, ensuring that full control does not come at the cost of platform capability.
